title: Lavender Tallow Balm: The Weird Beef Fat Thing That Fixed My Face
body:
Okay so. My skin. It’s a whole situation. It’s not oily, it’s not dry, it’s just… angry. For no reason. Like, I’d wake up and it’s tight. But also shiny in weird patches. By 3 PM it feels like I’m wearing a mask of sand. I tried the thing with the green bottle from the pharmacy. Made it worse. Tried that fancy French cream my friend swore by, the one that costs like a week’s groceries. Felt nice for five minutes. Then back to sand-face. I was at the end of my rope, you know? Just washing with water and hoping for the best. Which, for the record, is not a strategy. It was spring, everything’s blooming, and my face decided to be a flaky, red desert. Makes total sense.

Anyway. I kept seeing stuff about tallow balm. Beef fat. For your face. I’m not a crunchy person. I eat burgers, I don’t usually rub them on my cheeks. The whole thing sounded kind of medieval. Or like something my great-grandma would have had in a tin. But I was scrolling Etsy one night, couldn’t sleep, and this shop popped up. This whipped tallow balm. From France. Grass-fed cows, all that. And they had a lavender one. For sleep. My skin was bad, I wasn’t sleeping, it felt like a sign. Or just desperation. Same thing sometimes.

I ordered it. Why not.

## How Beef Tallow for Skin Stopped Feeling Weird

It showed up in this little jar. Cute packaging, honestly. I opened it. Smelled like… lavender. But real lavender. Not the candle aisle at Target. More like the plant my mom tried to grow that died. Earthy. Herbal. Kind of calming actually. The texture was the weird part. It’s whipped, so it’s like this fluffy, dense cream. You scoop a tiny bit and it melts the second it hits your skin. Like, instantly. Not greasy. Just… gone. But your skin feels different. Not oily. Just quiet.

Here’s the science bit I read after I bought it, because I was curious: tallow is kinda similar to the oils our own skin makes. Sebum, or whatever. So it absorbs deep, doesn’t just sit on top and clog everything up. This one’s whipped, which I guess makes it lighter. It made sense in a weird way. I was putting a hundred synthetic things on my face, maybe it just wanted something simple. Something… familiar. Even if it’s from a cow.

I started using it as a night cream. Just a tiny dab after I washed my face. The lavender smell is no joke—it’s that timeless herbal, sleepy-time smell. My brain would just go, “Oh. Bed.” Which was a nice bonus. My cat would stare at me from the pillow like, “You smell like a field.” Judgmental little guy.

## What This Lavender Tallow Balm Actually Did

I didn’t expect miracles. I really didn’t. But after like, four days? My skin wasn’t tight in the morning. That was the first thing. I’d wake up and my face felt like my face. Not a stretched canvas. That alone was huge. After a couple weeks, the random dry patches on my cheeks and forehead? Gone. The sandpaper feeling by afternoon? Never showed up. My skin just felt… even. Normal. Hydrated but not shiny.

I got brave and used it on my hands. I wash my hands a million times a day, they’re always cracked, especially in spring with all the pollen and weird weather. This stuff healed the cracks around my knuckles in like, two days. It’s now my go-to for chapped lips too. Just a tiny bit. Works better than any waxy stick I’ve ever bought.

The best tallow for my concern—which was just this chaotic, reactive, uncomfortable skin—turned out to be this simple lavender one. It didn’t “do” ten things. It did one thing really well: it made my skin calm down and act like healthy skin. It’s a natural moisturizer for skin that’s just plain pissed off at the modern world. I didn’t have to layer five products. Just this one balm at night. Sometimes a tiny bit in the morning if I felt dry.

## My Skin Now & Would I Buy It Again?

So yeah. I’m on my second jar now. I told my sister about it, who has actual eczema, and she’s trying it. I just… use it. It’s on my nightstand. The ritual of it is nice. The smell means bedtime. My skin is just… fine. Not perfect. I still get a zit if I eat too much pizza. But it’s not a daily battle anymore. It’s not something I think about all the time. That’s the real win.

It’s spring now. Rainy one minute, sunny the next. My skin used to freak out with every weather change. Now it just… handles it. I don’t know how else to say it. This tallow balm for my weird combo skin just works. It’s not magic. It’s just a really good, simple thing that my skin understood.

I got mine from this little Etsy shop that makes it in France. The jar lasts forever because you use so little. Feels good supporting a small thing, you know? Not some giant corporation.

## Quick Questions I Get Asked

**Is beef tallow good for your face?**
Sounds wild, but yeah. It’s similar to our skin’s own oils, so it absorbs deep and doesn’t usually clog pores. It’s like giving your skin something it already knows how to use. My face definitely thinks it’s good.

**Does tallow balm clog pores?**
Not in my experience. It’s the opposite—because it sinks in so fast, it doesn’t just sit on top. My skin feels clear. I was worried about that too, but it’s been fine. Better than fine.

**What does lavender tallow balm smell like?**
Like actual lavender plants. Not perfume. It’s herbal, a little earthy, really calming. It’s not sweet. It’s the smell that makes you take a deep breath and unwind. Perfect for a night cream.

Anyway. If your skin is being difficult, if nothing else is working, maybe give the weird beef fat thing a shot. I’m glad I did. My face is just… chill now. And I sleep better. Two wins.
